Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 558 AM EDT Mon Oct 26 2026

- Dry weather continues today through Thursday.  

- Temperatures remain at or slightly above normal today and Tuesday, 
despite a shallow cold front sagging southward across the region.  

- A low chance of fog or low clouds across the Thumb and Tri-Cities 
tonight and Tuesday morning. 

- A renewed warming trend begins Wednesday and Thursday as high 
temperatures return to the 70s. 

- The next chance for measurable rainfall holds off until Thursday 
night and Friday along the next weak cold front.

&&

.AVIATION...

A weak cold front will drop through the region early in the day. 
Cloud cover and southwesterly flow has presented an environment not 
as favorable for fog development this morning, with the obs cooling 
close to the dewpoints as of around 10Z which has allowed a few obs 
of 4-5 SM. Will keep an MVFR vsby for the Detroit tafs to start the 
period to give credit to the persistence of the fog over the last 
few days south of the front. The front will flip the winds around 
from SW to N today though speeds will remain under 10 knots, with 
further veering to NE or E tonight. HIgh clouds this morning will be 
gradually replaced by low VFR or MVFR cigs behind the front. Model 
soundings suggest the possibility of the low VFR clouds currently 
across northern lower will reach at least MBS and FNT during the 
morning before mixing out so they stand the best chance of MVFR for 
a few hours. Further south should largely hold VFR. 

D21/DTW Convection... Thunderstorms are not forecast through the TAF 
period.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low for cigs/vsby below 200 ft and/or 1/2SM this morning. 

* Low for cigs at or below 5000 ft today.

&&
